          # at/over its 262144-byte content cap (v1.0.538 died mid-upload,
          # after the tag + GitHub release). Fast-fail HERE, before staging
          # and publish, not at the server.
          bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md
          echo "publishable=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Verify tag matches pubspec version
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          echo "tag=$tag pubspec=$version"
          if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "Tag v$tag does not match pubspec version $version"
            exit 1
          fi

      # setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) provisions a publish-scoped credential for
      # the whole job: it exports PUB_TOKEN and registers
      # `dart pub token add https://pub.dev --env-var PUB_TOKEN`, so EVERY
      # pub.dev request — including `dart pub get` metadata reads — carries
      # the publish token. pub.dev rejects it on metadata reads
      # ("depends on ... which doesn't exist (authorization failed)",
      # exit 69; tag v0.1.340, run 34503923233). Resolution must run
      # unauthenticated: strip the credential, resolve, restore it only
      # for the publish step.
      - name: Strip publish credential for dependency resolution
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true

      - run: dart pub get
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'

      # The repo root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the pub
      # package (flutter_app with its 57 MB wasm toolchain, yoclip media,
      # browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs) — `dart publish`
      # packs everything under the root that isn't gitignored, which blew
      # the archive past pub.dev's hard 100 MB cap (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB,
      # "Content-length exceeds upper bound"). Publish from a staged copy
      # that carries only the package surface; the size guard makes any
      # future bloat a LOCI error instead of a pub.dev rejection.
      - name: Stage publishable package (sub-projects stay out)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/publish-stage
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub get)

      - name: Publish (automated publishing via OIDC)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          pkg=$(grep '^name:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          ver="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          served() { curl -fsSL "https://pub.dev/api/packages/$pkg" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.latest.version' || true; }
          # The push-run and release-run twins of the same tag both land here
          # (serialized by the job concurrency group): the loser must see the
          # version already served and exit green, not fail on a re-upload.
          if [ "$(served)" = "$ver" ]; then
            echo "::notice::pub.dev already serves $pkg $ver — nothing to publish"
            exit 0
          fi
          dart pub token add https://pub.dev --env-var PUB_TOKEN || true
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub publish --force)
          # Verify the upload actually landed (#554, #611): pub.dev CDN
          # propagation takes minutes (v0.1.411: upload accepted 05:00:39Z,
          # latest flipped 05:04Z — the old 5x3s poll sampled at ~16s, saw
          # the stale version, and hard-errored a healthy release). Poll
          # immediately (fast path when propagation is instant), then every
          # 30s for up to 11 min (server-quoted 10 min + margin) before
          # declaring a mismatch; a REAL failure after the full window
          # still fails loudly (#554's guard).
          ok=""
          deadline=$((SECONDS + 660))
          while :; do
            polled=$(served)
            echo "poll: pub.dev serves '$polled' (want $ver, t=${SECONDS}s)"
            if [ "$polled" = "$ver" ]; then ok=1; break; fi
            if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$deadline" ]; then break; fi
            sleep 30
          done
          if [ -z "$ok" ]; then
            echo "::error::tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME processed but pub.dev still serves '$(served)' after 11 min of polling — publish did not upload. Manual publish needed (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pub.dev verified: $pkg $ver"

  # Rehostable web SPA bundle (issue #1100): every release ships
  # fa-web-spa.zip — the release web build with <base href> rewritten to
  # ./, so it rehosts on any static host (incl. path-prefixed) or sandboxed
  # iframe with zero edits (docs/web-rehosting.md). Same build command AND
  # base-href as the Pages deploy; scripts/package_web_spa.sh patches the
  # tag on a COPY and enforces the absolute-path guard (AC3) before zipping.
  # Lives here, not in pages.yml: release commits (pubspec/CHANGELOG bumps)
  # fall outside pages.yml's path filters, so a Pages-produced bundle could
  # never attach to the actual release commit.
  web-spa:
    name: Build web SPA bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive asset: a web-build failure (guard trip, SDK flake) must NOT
    # hold the release hostage — CLI provenance (SHA256SUMS) and the vpinned
    # bump still ship. Job-level continue-on-error reports the job (and its
    # check) as SUCCESS — the failed steps stay visible on the run page for
    # the manual check. Downstream needs see success; the provenance fa-*
    # sweep then deterministically finds no zip (success -> signed,
    # failure -> absent — never a half-updated manifest).
    continue-on-error: true
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach fa-web-spa.zip to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as build-web / the release path (#281); EXACT patch
      # pin (#1431): a wildcard re-resolves a new engine build on every
      # 3.47.x patch and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the size
      # gates track. Bump consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile; a
        # pubspec/lockfile skew must fail the PR, not float.
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Same placeholders as the Pages job (both files are gitignored).
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch flutter_app/.env

      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web (release, Pages base)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter build web --release --base-href /app/

      # interpreter assets are mobile-only (loaded exclusively through
      # WasiSandboxShell under Android/iOS guards; the web sandbox boots
      # env_factory_stub -> MemoryShell -> CDN pyodide/quickjs), so zipping
      # them into fa-web-spa.zip would ship ~47 MB of dead weight.
      - name: Prune mobile-only wasm interpreter assets (#1096 AC3)
        run: rm -rf flutter_app/build/web/assets/assets/wasm

      - name: Package fa-web-spa.zip (relative base + AC3 guard)
        run: bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh flutter_app/build/web fa-web-spa.zip

      # AC1 (#1096): size manifest + +5% budget gate on the shipped SPA
      # zip. First run self-seeds web-spa.tsv (--init-if-missing) — the
      # step below uploads it for fetch+commit; committed floor afterwards.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-web-spa.zip)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check fa-web-spa.zip \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-spa.tsv --init-if-missing

      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1

        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --generate-notes \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true

      # release can then only be gated on a MISSING asset. Surface the miss

      # trips); the failed steps remain visible in the job view.

  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web
  # bundle cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering makes the fa-*
  # sweep deterministic — web-spa success -> zip signed, web-spa failure ->
  # zip absent — never a half-updated manifest.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')

      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Windows)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: '& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Fa\bin\fa.exe" --version'

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Unix)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -x "${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa" ]; then
            fa_path="${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa"
          else
            fa_path="$HOME/.local/bin/fa"
          fi
          # macOS downloads are quarantined by Gatekeeper; the installer strips
          # the attribute, but harden the smoke test in case it ever regresses.
          if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
            xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$fa_path" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
          "$fa_path" --version

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # gh-1172: the bump pushes DIRECTLY to protected main authenticated as the
    # fa-release-bot GitHub App — the only bypass actor on the main ruleset
    # (the PR stopgap from 2026-09-29 is retired: it burned a full CI queue
    # cycle + machine review round on every chore bump). The App token is
    # minted job-locally; nothing else in the repo can read RELEASE_APP_*.
    # release-tag below cuts the tag from the pushed commit. Scheduled runs
    # catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —
    # on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps the job's
    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): the App is the ruleset
          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — the bump touches a handful of files; every
          # historical blob is dead transfer weight.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed commit triggers the
          # follow-up ci.yml run whose release-tag job cuts the tag —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # gh-1299 NG1: the bump regenerates flutter_app/pubspec.lock in-commit
      # (the lockfile pins the parent path package version, so every bump
      # invalidates it) and refuses to ship while any inventory lockfile is
      # dirty — both need flutter on PATH. This job AUTHORS the lockfile for
      # every future release, so its SDK is pinned to the same 3.47.x the
      # consuming (--enforce-lockfile) build legs pin (PR #1304 rework
      # thread 8 — closes the author/consumer SDK drift class).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Bump version, changelog, push to main
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after.
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Same fa-release-bot App as the bump job (gh-1172): the tag push and
      # `gh release create` ride the App installation token — without an
      # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in tag_release.sh was a
      # guaranteed silent no-op and the curated CHANGELOG notes never reached
      # the release object (BLOCK finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write only —
          # the tag push + `gh release create` need nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      # gh-1299 NG2/AC3: the tag step smokes `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile`
      # on the bump commit BEFORE tagging/publishing (a release commit that
      # cannot resolve its own lockfile is never tagged, never published) —
      # the gate needs flutter on PATH, pinned to the same 3.47.x the
      # consuming build legs use (PR #1304 rework thread 8).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 1): warm the pub cache with the shared
      # bounded-retry action so tag_release.sh's own enforce-lockfile smoke
      # rides it — the smoke stays in the script (release_hygiene NG2/AC3
      # pins it) but is no longer the job's first resolution, so one
      # transient git-dep clone reset cannot abort the pre-tag gate on a
      # cold cache (the v1.0.516 build-macos exit-69 class, on the release
      # path).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Cut annotated tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # gh-1192 AC3: pin the tag to the bump commit the push event
          # carried. head_commit.id is frozen at event time; a default
          # checkout can land on a main that moved in the seconds between the
          # bump push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178
          # interloper that way). tag_release.sh validates the sha (exact
          # bump subject + matching pubspec version) before tagging and
          # refuses to tag a moving HEAD when nothing qualifies.
          BUMP_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
        run: bash scripts/tag_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi
